questionsApplications.label: Illustrative current innovation applications the programme uses to introduce prospective students to the field (fuel-saving aircraft coatings, hydrogen transport and logistics, making buildings and operations more sustainable, developing medicines, advising an energy company, medical apps for home blood-glucose monitoring, AI and sound-wave technology for cancer diagnosis, predicting pregnancy risks in remote areas)

Career and further-study trajectories the programme prepares graduates for (energy and sustainability careers, healthcare-innovation consulting, new-business development, technology consulting and investment, pharmaceutical and biotech innovation management, production-process innovation, starting a science-based company, environment and resource management, innovation management, complex-systems engineering and management, the award-winning sharkskin aircraft-coating project)

alternatives.concept: A science-and-business programme combines entrepreneurship, strategy, finance and empirical research with renewable-energy systems and biomedical science. Biochemistry, pharmacology and disease mechanisms provide a life-science strand; energy-system design, life-cycle analysis and sustainability governance provide an energy strand. Mathematics, programming and data analysis support technical and commercial inquiry. It offers a substantive interdisciplinary response while lacking VU’s dedicated physics and organic-chemistry sequence, integrated innovation-project progression and compulsory research internship.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for HCBLIFE213, HCBBIOM311, HCBBIOM313 and HCBBIOM312, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes BENENTR212 (semester 2), BENENTR311 and BENBUSI312 (semester 6), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD311 (semester 5) and BENECON312 (semester 6), which formally require it. DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes DISMATH211 (semester 3), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 2, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Programming, Sustainability Essentials I, Research Methods & Statistics) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (Pharmacology, Governance of Sustainability, Mechanisms of Disease, Infection & Immunity, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Market Research, Econometrics, Money Banking & Finance) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for HCBLIFE213, HCBBIOM311 (semester 3), HCBBIOM313, HCBBIOM312, HCBLIFE211 (semester 4) and HCBLIFE212, HCBLIFE311 (semester 5), and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. HCBGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for HCBPSYC311 (semester 5), and is scheduled before it. BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes BENENTR212 (semester 2), BENENTR311 and BENBUSI312 (semester 6), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD311 (semester 5) and BENECON312 (semester 6), which formally require it. DISGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes DISMATH211 (semester 3), which formally requires it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1/level-2 courses (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Biochemistry, Molecular Cell Biology, Human Physiology) are concentrated in semesters 1-4, and level-3 advanced work (Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Infection & Immunity, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Medical & Health Psychology, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Market Research, Econometrics, Money Banking & Finance) is concentrated in semesters 3-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

notes.text: UCR offers related science-and-business pathways. Biochemistry, laboratory methods, renewable-energy design and environmental chemistry contribute real science content. Dedicated physics, organic chemistry, diagnostic imaging and VU’s integrated innovation projects remain substantial differences.

VU includes a compulsory 24-EC research internship and 30 EC of approved electives. UCR’s scheduled 180 EC comprises taught courses; optional independent research is shown separately and does not reproduce the internship.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Science, Business & Innovation combines physical and life sciences with business, entrepreneurship and innovation projects. Energy and life science are recurring application domains. The Dutch program includes approved elective study and an individual research internship.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR pathways connect science with business: a combined energy and life-science pathway, an energy-focused pathway and a life-science-focused pathway. Physics, organic chemistry, diagnostic imaging and the compulsory internship differ substantially from VU.

curriculum.limitation: This 180-EC annual curriculum preserves 30 EC of approved elective or minor study. Course-specific participation, laboratory safety, Dutch-language clearance and tutoring requirements apply. The 24-EC research internship requires Research Design and Methodology and no more than 18 EC of other unfinished units. First-year study advice requires 42 EC; future annual regulations may change.
